THE 30-SECOND VERSION

Who holds the complete picture of a new hire’s readiness?

Coordinate across existing systems instead of replacing every system.

UAEinitial market
3strategy phases
B2BSaaS concept

Course strategy case study. Research scope and measurement limits are explained below.

01 / PROBLEM

The handoffs hold the risk

A new employee needs documents, approvals, equipment and system access. When each part lives in a different spreadsheet, inbox or ticket queue, no single team has a reliable view of readiness.

02 / CONTRIBUTION

What I worked on

I developed a strategy covering the initial customer group, problem focus, positioning, expansion logic, success measures and a three-year roadmap. The work also makes leadership questions and unresolved assumptions explicit.

03 / EVIDENCE

A defined starting customer

The proposal focuses on UAE companies with 200–1,500 employees and complex onboarding across entities. This is a strategic target segment, not a claim about an existing customer base or proven product-market fit.

04 / DECISION

Own the live status of each hire

Loop Work is positioned as a coordination layer above HR, identity and operational systems. Its initial job is to help a company get a person ready to work on day one.

05 / SOLUTION

Start narrow, expand with the workflow

The roadmap begins with UAE onboarding, then considers the wider employee lifecycle and Saudi expansion, followed by predictive delay insights once meaningful operating data exists.

06 / TRADEOFFS

Integration depth before broad reach

Regional specificity may create value, but integrations and policy dependencies take effort to maintain. The strategy should be revisited when engineering capacity, buyer priorities and integration feasibility are known.

07 / MEASUREMENT

Track readiness and repeat value

The product should be assessed through the onboarding outcome and sustained customer use, rather than how many checklists are created. The strategy document contains the detailed success framework; it does not report live customer results.

08 / LEARNING

Strategy depends on what must be true

A narrow initial market is only useful if the proposed coordination gap matters enough for a buyer to pay. Buyer discovery and integration validation should precede a broad platform commitment.
